hypotheses.statement:
For every integer $n\ge2$ there is a constant $L_n\ge1$ with the following property. Let $K\in\mathbb R$, and let $(X,d,\mathcal H_d^n)$ be a noncollapsed $\mathrm{RCD}(K,n)$ space. Let $p\in X$. If every pointed Gromov–Hausdorff tangent of $X$ at $p$ is pointed-isometric to $(\mathbb R^n,|\cdot|,0)$, then there exist an open neighborhood $U$ of $p$, an open set $V\subset\mathbb R^n$, and a homeomorphism $F:U\to V$ such that $$L_n^{-1}d(x,z)\le |F(x)-F(z)|\le L_nd(x,z)
 \qquad (x,z\in U).$$ The distance on the left and right is the original distance $d$ restricted to $U$.

Under the hypotheses of Theorem 1, there is an open set $\mathcal U\subset X$ containing every $n$-regular point, with $\mathcal H_d^n(X\setminus\mathcal U)=0$, and a countable atlas of $L_n$-bi-Lipschitz charts from ambient-open subsets of $\mathcal U$ onto open subsets of $\mathbb R^n$. Each chart uses the restricted ambient distance, and its transition maps are $L_n^2$-bi-Lipschitz.

Fix an $n$-regular point $p$ in the space of Theorem 1. There are rescalings $$(X_ u,d_ u,\mathfrak m_ u,p_ u) =(X,s_ u^{-1}d,s_ u^{-n}\mathcal H_d^n,p), \qquad s_ u\downarrow0,$$ numbers $\kappa_ u\downarrow0$, and radii $T_ u\uparrow\infty$ with $\kappa_ u T_ u^2 o0$, having the following properties. The space $X_ u$ is $\mathrm{RCD}(-\kappa_ u,n)$. For a sequence $\delta_ u\downarrow0$, all balls with center in $B_{64T_ u}(p_ u)$ and radius at most $64T_ u$ satisfy $$\label{co:uniform-flatness} \left| rac{\mathfrak m_ u(B_r(y))}{\omega_n r^n}-1 ight| \le\delta_ u, \qquad d_{GH} igl(\overline B_r(y),\overline B_r(0^n) igr) \le\delta_ u r.$$ There are harmonic columns $u_ u$ on $B_{32T_ u}(p_ u)$, converging on every fixed ball locally uniformly and strongly in $W^{1,2}$ to Euclidean coordinates, and $$\label{co:original-gradient-bound} | abla u_ u|\le C_n \quad ext{on }B_{16T_ u}(p_ u).$$

For each pair of fixed constants $A,C\ge1$, uniformly for $y\in B_A(p)$ and $i\ge0$, $$\label{co:small-mass}
 r_i^{2-n}M(B_{Cr_i}(y))\le o(1)R_i(y).$$

Fix a testing center $x$, and suppress it in the notation. Let $a>0$ in [co:slow-QH] be chosen so that $4a<\gamma$. Set $$B_i=H_{i+1}-H_i,\qquad \Delta_i=Q_i-Q_{i+1}, \qquad a_i=H_i\xi$$ for a fixed $\xi\in\mathbb R^n$. Then, uniformly for every integer $k\ge0$, $$\begin{aligned} &H_i\Delta_iH_i\le B_i\le(1+C\varepsilon_\nu)H_i\Delta_iH_i, \label{co:inverse-increment-order}\\ &\sum_{i

Let $\Omega$ be one of the bounded rescaled domains satisfying [pi:dirichlet-sobolev], and suppose that $h\in W^{1,2}_0(\Omega)$ is nonnegative and bounded, with $$\int\langle\nabla h,\nabla\psi\rangle\,\mathrm d\mathfrak m =\int\psi\,\mathrm d\mu$$ for compactly supported Lipschitz tests, where $\mu$ is a finite positive measure. If $\mu(\Omega)\le P$, then $$\int_\Omega|\nabla h|\,\mathrm d\mathfrak m\le CP, \qquad \int_\Omega|\nabla h|^2\,\mathrm d\mathfrak m\le\|h\|_\infty P. \label{pi:positive-source-bounds}$$ The constant in the first inequality depends only on the Sobolev constant, its exponent, and an upper bound for $\mathfrak m(\Omega)$.

There are nonnegative numbers $P_i(a)$, defined for every $a\in B_4(p)$ and $i\ge0$, with $$\sup_{a\in B_4(p)}\sum_{i=0}^{\infty}P_i(a)=o(1),
 \label{pi:poisson-sum}$$ and functions $f_i^a$ on $B_{8Sr_i}(a)$ such that, with $q^a=d_a^2/2$, $$\Delta f_i^a=a_i:=n+C_0\kappa r_i^2,
 \qquad f_i^a-q^a\in W^{1,2}_0(B_{8Sr_i}(a)).
 \label{pi:poisson-definition}$$ Here $C_0$ depends only on $n,S$ and is the same for every center and every scale. The following bounds hold: $$\begin{aligned}
 0\le q^a-f_i^a&\le Cr_i^2,
 &\sup_{B_{4Sr_i}(a)}|\nabla f_i^a|&\le Cr_i,
 \label{pi:poisson-boundedness}\\
 \int_{B_{8Sr_i}(a)}|\nabla(f_i^a-q^a)|^2\,\mathrm d\mathfrak m
 &\le Cr_i^{n+2}P_i(a),
 &\int_{B_{8Sr_i}(a)}|\nabla(f_i^a-q^a)|\,\mathrm d\mathfrak m
 &\le Cr_i^{n+1}P_i(a),
 \label{pi:poisson-errors}\\
 \mathcal B_\kappa(f_i^a,1)(B_{2Sr_i}(a))
 &\le Cr_i^nP_i(a).
 \label{pi:poisson-shifted-mass}
\end{aligned}$$

Suppose that $f$ has constant Laplacian and $a$ is harmonic on a ball on which both functions have bounded gradients. Put $g_a=\langle
abla f,
abla aangle$. For interior Sobolev tests $\phi\in W^{1,2}_0$ one has $$\int\langle
abla g_a,
abla\phiangle\,\mathrm d\mathfrak m
 =2\int(\operatorname{Hess}f-g)(
abla a,
abla\phi)\,\mathrm d\mathfrak m.
 \label{pi:weak-cancellation-equation}$$ The identity is local, with the right side interpreted on a slightly larger interior ball if a cutoff is needed.

There are functions $E_i(a)>0$, for $a\in B_4(p)$, such that $$E_i(a)\ge P_i(a),\qquad
 \sup_a\sum_{i=0}^\infty E_i(a)=o(1),\qquad
 \inf_a E_i(a)>0\quad\hbox{for each fixed }i.
 \label{pi:pinching-summability}$$ Let $T=R_i(y)^{-1/2}$ with $d(a,y)\le C_{\mathrm{sep}}r_i$, and put $U=T(u-u(a))/r_i$. In the metric $r_i^{-1}d$, with $\widehat f_i^a=f_i^a/r_i^2$, there is a matrix $A_i^a(T)$ satisfying $\|A_i^a(T)-\mathrm{Id}\|=o(1)$ and $$\left\|\langle\nabla\widehat f_i^a,\nabla U\rangle
       -A_i^a(T)(U-U(a))\right\|_{W^{1,2}(B_{S/2}(a))}
 \le C\sqrt{E_i(a)}.
 \label{pi:radial-invariance-equation}$$ The ball and all derivatives in this display use the rescaled metric. Arbitrary additive constants may be used in $U$.

On $B_{8R}(z)$ one has $$\Delta v=0,\qquad
 |\nabla v|\le C,\qquad
 M(v)(B_{8R}(z))\le Cs^2,
 \label{pi:pair-poisson-bounds}$$ and $$\|h-(U(x)-U(z))\|_{L^2(B_{8R}(z))}\le Cs.
 \label{pi:constant-direction}$$

Work in the rescaled units above. Suppose that $w$ is a bounded Sobolev function on $B_{4R}(z)$ with $\|w\|_\infty\le C_1$, and that $$L_zw=w+\ell\cdot U+k+e_w,
 \qquad \|e_w\|_{L^2(B_{4R}(z))}\le C_1s.
 \label{pi:transport-hypothesis}$$ Put $\alpha=\|w\|_{L^2(B_R(z))}$. If $|\ell|+|k|\le C_1(\alpha+s)$, then $$\|w\|_{L^2(B_{2R}(z))}\le C(\alpha+s),
 \label{pi:transport-conclusion}$$ where $C$ is independent of $\alpha,s$. The constants may depend on $C_1$ and the already fixed radii and coordinate bounds.

For all sufficiently late spaces, there is a vector $b\in\mathbb R^n$ with $|b|\le C$ such that $$\|\nabla(v-b\cdot U)\|_{L^2(B_{2L+4}(y))}\le Cs. \label{pi:sharp-projection-equation}$$ The constants and the late-space threshold are uniform in the configuration [pi:center-configuration] and the dyadic scale.

For every fixed $L,C_{\mathrm{sep}}>1$, the functions $E_i$ may be chosen as in [pi:definition-E], with the uniform summability and positive floors in [pi:pinching-summability], so that the following holds for all sufficiently late spaces. Define $$D_{i,y}=R_i(y)^{-1} \bigl[r_i^{2-n}M(u)(B_{Lr_i}(y))\bigr]R_i(y)^{-1}.$$ For every configuration [pi:center-configuration], $$D_{i,y}[u(x)-u(z)] \le Cr_i^2\bigl(E_i(x)+E_i(z)\bigr). \label{pi:directional-estimate}$$ The same functions work simultaneously for all such centers and all dyadic scales. All enlargement constants are fixed before choosing the late-space threshold.

At $P=P_x$, $x\in B_1(p)$, write $r=r_i$, $H=H_i(x)$, $Q=Q_i(x)$, $Z=Z_i(x)$, $S=S_i(x)$, and $E=E_i(x)$. There is a linear error $e(\xi)$ such that $$\begin{aligned}
 r^{-1}|v_i|_Q&\le C\sqrt\varepsilon\sqrt E,
       \label{re:field-value}\\
 (\mathrm Dv_i)\xi&=S\xi+e(\xi),
       \label{re:field-linear}\\
 |S\xi|_Q&\le\sqrt\varepsilon\sqrt{Z[\xi]},
       &|e(\xi)|_Q&\le C\sqrt\varepsilon\sqrt E\,|\xi|_H,
       \label{re:field-small-linear}\\
 |\xi^Te(\xi)|&\le C\sqrt{Z[\xi]E}\,|\xi|_H,
       \label{re:field-diagonal}\\
 r|\mathrm D^2v_i(\xi,\xi)|_Q
       &\le C\left(\sqrt{Z[\xi]}\,|\xi|_H
                          +\sqrt E\,|\xi|_H^2\right).
       \label{re:field-second}
\end{aligned}$$ There is a fixed $C_v\ge1$ such that, in every order $m\ge0$, $$\label{re:field-jets}
 r_i^{m-1}\|\mathrm D^m v_i(P_x)\|_{H_i(x)\to Q_i(x)}
       \le\varepsilon C_v^{m+1}(m!)^s.$$

Choose $B\ge C_v$ sufficiently large and then $\varepsilon$ sufficiently small, depending on $A,\sigma,B$ and the fixed data. If [re:metric-bootstrap] and [re:jet-bootstrap] hold at level $i$, the update [re:iteration] satisfies [re:jet-bootstrap] at level $i+1$. This assertion does not require the new-level metric bound.

There are fixed $A,B$ and a sufficiently small flatness threshold such that the maps [re:iteration] are smooth on all of $\Omega$ for every finite $i$, their Jacobians are invertible there, and [re:metric-bootstrap]–[re:jet-bootstrap] hold for all $x\in B_1(p)$ and every $i$.

For sufficiently flat data in the preceding construction, there is $\rho>0$ such that the uniform limit $$F(x)=\lim_{i\to\infty}h_i(u(x)),\qquad x\in B_1(p),$$ restricts to a bi-Lipschitz homeomorphism from $B_\rho(p)$ onto an open subset of $\mathbb R^n$. Its distance comparisons use the ambient distance $d$ restricted to $B_\rho(p)$.
